speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: The list says the children's hose, before Bartholomew Fair. Look at them. Do not buy a story about them.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: Mine are whole at the heel. Judith's are not, and she will not stand still to be told so.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Then they are looked at. Whole, and not whole. Nothing is bought this morning.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am looking. I am not pricing. The fair is not this week.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: Bartholomew Fair is a date, when it is a date. Today is only hose on a bench.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: Hamnet's have a thin place at the knee. He says it is the running. He is not wrong, and I am not buying him a pair with my mouth.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Nobody is buying. The list said look. The list has been obeyed.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then the morning is the looking. I have nothing to put on a stall for it.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: And nothing to walk the town for. A bench in this house is the whole of the errand.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: Judith will want the thin heel made into a tale. It is a thin heel. It can wait on a stitch.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Joan can stitch a heel without a fair being cried for it. Leave the fair where the calendar keeps it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not crying a fair, and I am not naming a house to put the hose in. Hose are hose.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: Good. A house was not on the list. The list was hose, and you have looked.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: Three children, three reports. Whole, thin, and running. That is the morning's arithmetic, and it spends nothing.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Spends nothing. Remember that at four o'clock, if four o'clock has a lap in it. This morning does not.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: This morning has a bench and three pairs of hose. I have seen them. I am not mending them with money.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: Then fold them back into the chest. Looking is done when the lid is down.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: I will tell Judith her heel was seen, and that nobody made a speech long enough to hide it.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Tell her at dinner. The bench is clear.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The bench is clear. I looked. I did not buy. I did not go out to look at anything larger.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: Larger can keep. The chest has what the children wear, and that was the question.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: And it is answered. Whole enough to wait, thin enough to stitch, and nothing bought to settle an argument.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Nothing bought. I can say that twice and still have said only the one thing.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: Then say it once more and go and be useful at something that is not a stall.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Useful, and indoors. The town has had you on a ladder's errand already this week.
